title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate
description: Validates ability to design and implement secure and robust solutions using AWS technologies and Well-Architected Framework pillars.

questions.statement: A company hosts a static website on Amazon S3 and distributes the content globally via Amazon CloudFront. The security team requires users to access files exclusively through the CloudFront URL and never directly through the S3 bucket endpoint. What is the recommended configuration?

options.text: Configure Origin Access Control (OAC) on the CloudFront distribution and update the S3 bucket policy to allow access only from that distribution.
options.explanation: Correct: OAC is the current secure AWS recommendation to restrict S3 bucket access solely to designated CloudFront distributions.

options.text: Make the S3 bucket public and block direct traffic using Security Group rules.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 buckets do not use Security Groups.

options.text: Use Pre-signed URLs for all public page read requests.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Pre-signed URLs are intended for restricted temporary access, not public static websites.

options.text: Create an S3 VPC Endpoint and route CloudFront distribution into a private subnet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudFront is a global edge service and does not run inside private VPC subnets.

questions.generalExplanation: Origin Access Control (OAC) supersedes legacy OAI and enables Amazon CloudFront to authenticate with S3 buckets via SigV4, completely restricting direct public access to S3.

questions.statement: An application running on Amazon EC2 connects to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Corporate compliance mandates that database passwords must be rotated automatically every 30 days without manual intervention or application downtime. Which solution satisfies this requirement?

options.text: Store the database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager and enable automatic rotation using the built-in Secrets Manager rotation Lambda function.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Secrets Manager natively integrates with Amazon RDS to rotate secrets on a scheduled basis using pre-configured Lambda rotation templates.

options.text: Store the credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store standard string parameters and update them manually each month.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Parameter Store standard strings do not provide native automated scheduled rotation for RDS.

options.text: Hardcode the password in the EC2 User Data script and reboot the instances every 30 days.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Hardcoding credentials in User Data is an insecure anti-pattern and disrupts instances.

options.text: Store credentials in an Amazon S3 bucket with versioning and enable S3 Lifecycle transitions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Lifecycle does not interact with the RDS database to rotate its internal password.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Secrets Manager enables automated password rotation for Amazon RDS with built-in Lambda rotation functions, updating both the database and stored secrets seamlessly.

questions.statement: A financial firm must store encrypted sensitive records in Amazon S3. The company must manage their own encryption keys, track every time a key is used in an audit log, and have the ability to immediately revoke access to the key. Which encryption option meets these requirements?

options.text: Server-Side Encryption with Customer Managed Keys stored in AWS KMS (SSE-KMS).
options.explanation: Correct: SSE-KMS with Customer Managed Keys gives full control over key policies, rotation, immediate key disabling, and logs every key usage event in AWS CloudTrail.

options.text: Server-Side Encryption with Amazon S3-Managed Keys (SSE-S3).
options.explanation: Incorrect: SSE-S3 uses AWS-owned keys that do not allow customer auditing or customer-initiated revocation.

options.text: Client-Side Encryption with unencrypted plaintext keys stored in Amazon DynamoDB.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Plaintext key storage is insecure and lacks KMS governance.

options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval with default vault access.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Glacier vault access does not provide key auditability like KMS.

questions.generalExplanation: SSE-KMS with Customer Managed Keys provides granular access control, key rotation management, and detailed audit trails in AWS CloudTrail for every decryption request.

questions.statement: An application running on private EC2 instances in a VPC needs to upload large data files to an Amazon S3 bucket. Security policies dictate that traffic must not traverse the public internet or use NAT Gateways. Which solution should the Solutions Architect implement?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint and update the route tables of the private subnets.
options.explanation: Correct: Gateway VPC Endpoints provide private routing to Amazon S3 directly over the AWS private network without internet gateways, NAT devices, or additional cost.

options.text: Attach an Internet Gateway to the VPC and assign public Elastic IPs to private instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: This exposes instances to the public internet, violating the security policy.

options.text: Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN from the VPC to the S3 public IP endpoint.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 is an AWS regional service, not an on-premises remote network reachable via Site-to-Site VPN.

options.text: Deploy a Fleet of NAT Instances across two public subnets.
options.explanation: Incorrect: NAT instances route traffic over the public internet, violating policy.

questions.generalExplanation: Gateway VPC Endpoints allow resources in private subnets to communicate with Amazon S3 over private AWS network infrastructure without requiring NAT Gateways or Internet Gateways.

questions.statement: A developer is writing code on an Amazon EC2 instance that reads messages from Amazon SQS and writes records to Amazon DynamoDB. How should the credentials be provided to the application securely?

options.text: Attach an IAM Role with appropriate SQS and DynamoDB permissions to the EC2 instance profile.
options.explanation: Correct: IAM instance profiles supply temporary credentials automatically rotated by the instance metadata service (IMDS), avoiding hardcoded keys.

options.text: Save the AWS access key and secret access key in a config file inside the Git repository.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storing credentials in source code or Git repositories is a major security risk.

options.text: Store the IAM user credentials in the instance user-data startup script.
options.explanation: Incorrect: User-data scripts are visible in plaintext to anyone with ec2:DescribeInstances permissions.

options.text: Create an IAM group and add the EC2 instance ID directly to the group.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Instances cannot be added to IAM groups; instances assume IAM Roles via Instance Profiles.

questions.generalExplanation: Attaching an IAM Role to an EC2 instance profile is the AWS Well-Architected standard for granting applications secure, temporary access to AWS services.

questions.statement: A web application behind an Application Load Balancer is receiving malicious automated SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. Which solution should be implemented to block these attacks at the edge?

options.text: Associate AWS WAF with the Application Load Balancer and enable AWS Managed Rules for SQL database and Core rule sets.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS WAF inspects layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS traffic and blocks SQLi, XSS, and common vulnerabilities using managed or custom rules.

options.text: Configure Network ACLs to block incoming traffic on TCP port 443.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Blocking port 443 on NACLs would block all legitimate HTTPS traffic.

options.text: Deploy Amazon GuardDuty to automatically terminate the EC2 instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: GuardDuty is a detective threat service; it does not filter layer 7 web traffic on ALBs.

options.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs on all public subnets.
options.explanation: Incorrect: VPC Flow Logs capture network metadata for analysis, but do not actively block layer 7 payloads.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS WAF integrated with an ALB or CloudFront inspects HTTP/S requests against rules (such as AWS Managed Rules for SQLi/XSS) to block malicious traffic before reaching compute servers.

questions.statement: An organization manages 30 AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The security team mandates that no account administrator should be able to launch EC2 instances outside of the eu-west-1 and us-east-1 regions. How can this be centrally enforced?

options.text: Apply a Service Control Policy (SCP) at the root OU denying ec2:* actions with a condition StringNotEquals on aws:RequestedRegion for eu-west-1 and us-east-1.
options.explanation: Correct: SCPs enforce preventive guardrails across all member accounts that even local account root users cannot override.

options.text: Configure an IAM boundary in the master account and attach it to an S3 bucket policy.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 bucket policies do not restrict EC2 regional instance launching.

options.text: Create an AWS Config rule in each account with manual remediation scripts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Config is detective rather than preventive; it does not block the API call.

options.text: Delete all default VPCs in unauthorized regions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Deleting default VPCs does not prevent users from creating custom VPCs and launching instances.

questions.generalExplanation: Service Control Policies (SCPs) in AWS Organizations provide central enforcement of region restrictions using the aws:RequestedRegion condition key.

questions.statement: A company is building a mobile gaming app that allows millions of players to register, log in with social providers (Apple, Google, Facebook), and obtain temporary scoped AWS credentials to upload screenshots directly to Amazon S3. Which AWS service provides this functionality?

options.text: Amazon Cognito User Pools and Identity Pools (Federated Identities)
options.explanation: Correct: Cognito User Pools manage user directory and social sign-in; Identity Pools exchange tokens for temporary AWS IAM credentials to access AWS resources directly.

options.text: AWS IAM Identity Center with SAML 2.0 assertions for each mobile phone
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM Identity Center is designed for corporate workforce SSO, not external consumer mobile apps.

options.text: AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory
options.explanation: Incorrect: Active Directory is an enterprise directory service, unsuitable for consumer mobile social federation.

options.text: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
options.explanation: Incorrect: Session Manager is for managing EC2 instance shell sessions.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Cognito handles consumer authentication (User Pools) and federated authorization (Identity Pools) to securely provide temporary AWS credentials for mobile and web applications.

questions.statement: A company wants to enable HTTPS encryption for their global public website hosted on Amazon CloudFront with a custom domain name (e.g., app.example.com). Which service should they use to request and manage the free SSL/TLS certificate, and in which AWS Region must it be provisioned?

options.text: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 (N. Virginia) region.
options.explanation: Correct: CloudFront distributions require custom SSL/TLS certificates to be provisioned in ACM specifically in the us-east-1 (N. Virginia) region.

options.text: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in any local region where the backend EC2 is located.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudFront is a global service and requires certificates to be requested in us-east-1.

options.text: AWS KMS in us-west-2.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS KMS creates cryptographic keys, not public SSL/TLS web certificates.

options.text: AWS Secrets Manager in eu-central-1.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Secrets Manager stores secrets, it does not issue public SSL certificates.

questions.generalExplanation: To use an ACM certificate with Amazon CloudFront, you must request or import the certificate in the US East (N. Virginia) region (us-east-1).

questions.statement: An enterprise requires 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT), financial protection against bill spikes caused by DDoS attacks, and advanced layer 3, 4, and 7 DDoS mitigation. Which service should they subscribe to?

options.text: AWS Shield Advanced
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Shield Advanced provides expanded DDoS protection, 24/7 DRT engagement, financial cost spike protection, and bundled AWS WAF support.

options.text: AWS Shield Standard
options.explanation: Incorrect: Shield Standard is basic automatic protection included for all customers without DRT support or cost protection.

options.text: Amazon GuardDuty
options.explanation: Incorrect: GuardDuty detects security anomalies, not active DDoS attack mitigation.

options.text: AWS CloudHSM
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudHSM is a cryptographic key hardware appliance.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Shield Advanced provides enterprise-grade DDoS mitigation with 24/7 DRT assistance and DDoS cost protection against scaling spikes.

questions.statement: An auditor in Account A needs temporary read-only access to Amazon S3 buckets located in Account B. What is the most secure method to grant this cross-account access without creating long-term IAM users in Account B?

options.text: Create an IAM Role in Account B with an S3 ReadOnly policy and a trust policy that permits Account A to assume the role via AWS STS.
options.explanation: Correct: Cross-account IAM roles with trust relationships allow users from another account to assume temporary credentials securely.

options.text: Create an IAM user in Account B with static access keys and email the keys to the auditor.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Creating static keys and emailing them is an insecure practice.

options.text: Make all S3 buckets in Account B public with read-only bucket policies.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Making buckets public exposes sensitive data to the entire world.

options.text: Configure VPC Peering between the default VPCs of both accounts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: VPC Peering establishes network connectivity, not IAM authorization to S3.

questions.generalExplanation: Cross-account access in AWS is best accomplished by defining an IAM role in the target account with a trust policy specifying the trusted account ID.

questions.statement: A Solutions Architect needs to implement automated compliance checks against CIS AWS Foundations Benchmarks across multiple AWS accounts and receive unified findings. Which service meets this requirement with the least effort?

options.text: AWS Security Hub
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Security Hub provides automated security checks against standard benchmarks such as the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark and AWS Foundational Security Best Practices.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail Insights
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudTrail Insights identifies anomalous API call volume, not configuration compliance standards.

options.text: Amazon Athena
options.explanation: Incorrect: Athena requires writing and maintaining custom SQL queries on log files.

options.text: AWS CodeDeploy
options.explanation: Incorrect: CodeDeploy automates application software deployments.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Security Hub provides built-in automated security standard checks including CIS AWS Foundations Benchmarks and PCI-DSS compliance.

questions.statement: How can an administrator ensure that no Amazon S3 bucket within an entire AWS account can ever be accidentally configured with public access, overriding individual bucket policies?

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 Block Public Access at the AWS Account level.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Block Public Access at the account level applies account-wide settings that block public access across all existing and future buckets in that account.

options.text: Configure an Amazon S3 Lifecycle rule to expire public objects after 1 day.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Lifecycle rules delete objects over time, but do not prevent public read access.

options.text: Delete the S3 VPC Endpoint from the VPC route table.
options.explanation: Incorrect: This affects VPC private routing, not public S3 bucket permissions.

options.text: Add a deny rule in the subnet Network ACL for TCP port 80.
options.explanation: Incorrect: NACLs do not control S3 bucket public permissions.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Block Public Access provides account-level centralized controls to ensure that objects never have public access regardless of how buckets are created.

questions.statement: A company wants to manage and access their private EC2 instances via shell terminal without opening inbound SSH port 22 in security groups, without maintaining bastion hosts, and without assigning public IP addresses. Which feature should they use?

options.text: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
options.explanation: Correct: Session Manager provides secure, one-click shell access to EC2 instances via the SSM Agent over HTTPS without opening inbound ports or managing SSH keys.

options.text: EC2 Instance Connect with open port 22
options.explanation: Incorrect: EC2 Instance Connect still requires inbound SSH access on port 22.

options.text: AWS Direct Connect
options.explanation: Incorrect: Direct Connect is a physical dedicated network link.

options.text: Amazon API Gateway with Lambda Authorizers
options.explanation: Incorrect: API Gateway is for REST/WebSocket APIs, not interactive server shell sessions.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager enables secure instance management through TLS connections over outbound port 443 via the SSM agent, eliminating the need for open inbound ports, bastion hosts, or SSH keys.

questions.statement: What happens to data previously encrypted with an AWS KMS Customer Managed Key (CMK) when automatic annual key rotation is enabled?

options.text: KMS saves the previous key material to seamlessly decrypt old ciphertext while using the new key material to encrypt new data.
options.explanation: Correct: KMS preserves old key versions backing the CMK, so data encrypted under older versions is decrypted automatically without manual re-encryption.

options.text: All existing ciphertext must be immediately decrypted and re-encrypted manually within 24 hours.
options.explanation: Incorrect: KMS automatically tracks and uses the appropriate key material version.

options.text: Old data becomes permanently corrupted unless copied to an unencrypted S3 bucket.
options.explanation: Incorrect: KMS retains previous key versions indefinitely to support decryption.

options.text: A new CMK ARN is generated and all IAM policies must be updated.
options.explanation: Incorrect: The CMK Key ID and ARN remain unchanged during rotation.

questions.generalExplanation: When KMS automatic key rotation is enabled, KMS generates new cryptographic material annually while retaining previous versions to decrypt data seamlessly without changing the Key ID or ARN.

questions.statement: A security operations team wants to be notified immediately and trigger automated remediation (such as isolating an infected EC2 instance) whenever Amazon GuardDuty detects a cryptocurrency mining finding. Which architectural pattern achieves this?

options.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches GuardDuty finding events and targets an AWS Lambda function to perform isolation.
options.explanation: Correct: GuardDuty sends finding events to EventBridge in near real-time, which can trigger Lambda functions for automated response and SNS for alerting.

options.text: Configure Amazon S3 Lifecycle rules on GuardDuty log exports to run daily Python scripts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Lifecycle manages object storage expiration, not real-time event triggering.

options.text: Create an AWS CloudFormation stack that polls GuardDuty APIs every 6 hours.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudFormation provisions resources, it does not poll APIs for security alerts.

options.text: Attach an IAM policy directly to GuardDuty with Deny permissions on EC2.
options.explanation: Incorrect: GuardDuty is an analysis service, not an IAM entity with policy attachments.

questions.generalExplanation: The event-driven pattern of Amazon GuardDuty -> Amazon EventBridge -> AWS Lambda / Amazon SNS provides automated, real-time threat detection and incident remediation.

questions.statement: A legal archive must store documents in Amazon S3 Glacier under a strict WORM (Write Once, Read Many) compliance policy. The policy must prevent any user, including account administrators and root, from modifying or deleting archives for 10 years. Which feature satisfies this requirement?

options.text: S3 Glacier Vault Lock policy
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Glacier Vault Lock allows you to deploy and lock compliance controls on individual vaults, making the policy immutable once locked.

options.text: Amazon S3 Access Points with public read permissions
options.explanation: Incorrect: Access Points do not enforce immutable WORM retention against root deletion.

options.text: AWS IAM Boundary with MFA Delete on EC2
options.explanation: Incorrect: MFA Delete applies to versioned S3 buckets, but does not lock Glacier vaults against root policy alterations like Vault Lock.

options.text: AWS KMS multi-region keys without key rotation
options.explanation: Incorrect: KMS keys manage encryption, not immutable WORM vault locking.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Glacier Vault Lock allows you to easily set and enforce compliance controls on individual S3 Glacier vaults with a Vault Lock policy that cannot be overwritten or deleted once locked.

questions.statement: How can a DevOps team automatically scan container images for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) as soon as images are pushed to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR)?

options.text: Enable Amazon Inspector automated scanning for Amazon ECR repositories.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon Inspector provides automated continuous vulnerability scanning for container images stored in Amazon ECR upon push.

options.text: Run an Amazon CloudSearch crawler on the container registry every midnight.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudSearch is a search engine, not a CVE vulnerability scanner.

options.text: Attach AWS WAF rules to the Amazon ECR endpoint.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS WAF inspects web traffic on ALBs/CloudFront, not container image layers.

options.text: Use AWS Storage Gateway Volume mode.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage Gateway is a hybrid cloud storage appliance.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Inspector integrates natively with Amazon ECR to automatically assess container images for operating system and programming language package vulnerabilities on push.

questions.statement: An organization must prove to external auditors that CloudTrail log files stored in an Amazon S3 bucket have not been modified, tampered with, or deleted since they were delivered by CloudTrail. Which feature should they enable?

options.text: CloudTrail Log File Integrity Validation
options.explanation: Correct: CloudTrail Log File Integrity Validation uses SHA-256 hashing and digital signatures with digest files to detect if log files have been modified or deleted.

options.text: Amazon S3 Object Tags
options.explanation: Incorrect: Object tags are simple key-value pairs that can be altered and do not validate cryptographic file integrity.

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights query
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudWatch Insights is a log querying tool, not a cryptographic hash validator.

options.text: Amazon EBS snapshot copy
options.explanation: Incorrect: EBS snapshots are volume backups, not S3 log file integrity validators.

questions.generalExplanation: CloudTrail log file integrity validation enables you to determine whether a log file was modified, deleted, or unchanged after CloudTrail delivered it.

questions.statement: A company requires stateful inspection, outbound URL/domain filtering (allowing only approved external domains), and intrusion prevention (IPS) for all traffic exiting their Amazon VPC to the internet. Which service meets this requirement?

options.text: AWS Network Firewall
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Network Firewall provides stateful layer 3-7 inspection, Suricata-compatible IPS rules, and outbound domain list filtering across VPC subnets.

options.text: Standard Network ACLs
options.explanation: Incorrect: Network ACLs are stateless layer 4 firewalls and cannot inspect domain names or provide IPS capabilities.

options.text: AWS Shield Standard
options.explanation: Incorrect: Shield Standard provides DDoS mitigation, not outbound domain filtering or IPS.

options.text: AWS Config
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Config is an auditing service for resource configurations.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Network Firewall is a stateful managed network firewall and intrusion detection/prevention service that supports 5-tuple filtering, domain allowlists, and deep packet inspection.

questions.statement: An order processing application experiences unpredictable traffic spikes. Each order takes an average of 2 minutes to process. Solutions architects need to decouple the web tier from the backend processing tier to ensure no orders are dropped during spikes and the backend scales automatically based on demand. Which TWO options meet these requirements? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use an Amazon SQS queue between the web tier and the order processing tier.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon SQS decouples components and durably buffers messages until consumers can process them.

options.text: Configure a Target Tracking Scaling Policy on the worker Auto Scaling group based on the customized SQS metric ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible.
options.explanation: Correct: Scaling based on queue depth backlog per instance ensures capacity scales proportionally to pending message volume.

options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer with sticky sessions directly to the processing instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Sticky sessions do not decouple tiers and may overload specific worker nodes.

options.text: Configure Amazon SNS topics with synchronous HTTP delivery to backend servers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SNS HTTP delivery does not provide a durable buffering queue if workers are temporarily overwhelmed.

options.text: Replace the backend with Spot EC2 instances in a fixed-size Auto Scaling group without an intermediate queue.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Spot instances can be interrupted and fixed size cannot handle unpredictable traffic bursts without a buffer.

questions.generalExplanation: The standard AWS architectural pattern for resilient asynchronous decoupling is using Amazon SQS queues with EC2 Auto Scaling groups scaled according to queue backlog depth per instance.

questions.statement: A company deploys an active-passive disaster recovery architecture across two AWS Regions: us-east-1 (Primary) and us-west-2 (Secondary). How should Amazon Route 53 be configured to automatically direct all user traffic to the secondary region if the primary region health checks fail?

options.text: Configure a Failover Routing policy with health checks pointing to the primary and secondary endpoints.
options.explanation: Correct: Route 53 Failover Routing is purpose-built for active-passive setups, routing to primary when healthy and automatically switching to secondary when primary fails health checks.

options.text: Configure a Simple Routing policy with two A records.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Simple routing returns multiple values in random order without automated health-check failover.

options.text: Configure a Geolocation Routing policy based solely on client IP location.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Geolocation routes by location, not automatic failure status.

options.text: Configure Multi-Value Answer routing without health checks.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Multi-value answer without health checks returns unhealthy IPs to clients.

questions.generalExplanation: Route 53 Failover Routing uses health checks to automatically redirect traffic from an unhealthy primary site to a healthy secondary disaster recovery site.

questions.statement: An Amazon RDS MySQL database requires high availability and automatic failover in the event of an underlying hardware failure or Availability Zone outage. How can this be accomplished with minimal administrative intervention?

options.text: Enable Multi-AZ deployment on the Amazon RDS instance.
options.explanation: Correct: RDS Multi-AZ synchronously replicates data to a standby instance in a different AZ and automatically fails over within 60-120 seconds if an outage occurs.

options.text: Create an asynchronous Read Replica in the same Availability Zone.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Read Replicas are asynchronous and require manual promotion during a disaster.

options.text: Take daily manual DB snapshots and copy them to S3.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Snapshots take hours to restore and do not provide automated failover.

options.text: Configure an AWS Lambda script to export database tables to DynamoDB every 15 minutes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exporting to DynamoDB is an expensive, custom, non-relational workaround.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployments provide enhanced availability and durability by automatically creating a synchronous standby copy in a different Availability Zone with automatic failover.

questions.statement: A business-critical web application uses Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Solutions Architects must design the database tier for high availability and near-zero recovery time objective (RTO) during primary instance failures. Which configuration is recommended?

options.text: Deploy Aurora with at least one Aurora Replica in a different Availability Zone with priority tier 0.
options.explanation: Correct: Aurora replicates storage across 3 AZs by default; adding an Aurora Replica in another AZ enables automatic failover in under 30 seconds without data loss.

options.text: Deploy a single Aurora instance and enable AWS Backup daily snapshots.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Single instance Aurora requires launching a new instance during failures, increasing RTO.

options.text: Export data continuously to Amazon S3 via Kinesis Data Firehose.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 export does not serve as an active relational database failover node.

options.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) to replicate data to an on-premises server.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Replicating to on-premises increases latency and failover complexity.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Aurora automatically fails over to an existing Aurora Replica in another AZ in less than 30 seconds when the primary writer instance fails.

questions.statement: A regulatory agency requires an insurance company to maintain copies of all submitted claim documents in two different geographical regions at least 500 miles apart to protect against regional disasters. Which Amazon S3 feature should be configured?

options.text: Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) with S3 Versioning enabled on source and destination buckets.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 CRR automatically and asynchronously replicates objects across buckets in different AWS Regions when versioning is enabled on both buckets.

options.text: Amazon S3 Same-Region Replication (SRR) with default encryption.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SRR replicates within the same region, failing the 500-mile geographic separation requirement.

options.text: Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering with archive tiering.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Intelligent-Tiering changes storage classes within the same bucket, not across regions.

options.text: AWS DataSync running once every 30 days.
options.explanation: Incorrect: A 30-day periodic sync fails real-time regulatory compliance requirements.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) replicates objects (and metadata/tags) continuously between buckets in different AWS Regions to satisfy geographic compliance.

questions.statement: An e-commerce application runs on EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. During a flash sale, the ALB marks several instances unhealthy due to CPU saturation, but the Auto Scaling group does not terminate and replace them because it only evaluates EC2 status checks. What should the architect change?

options.text: Change the Auto Scaling group health check type from EC2 to ELB.
options.explanation: Correct: Configuring the ASG health check type to ELB ensures the Auto Scaling group replaces instances that fail ALB HTTP/HTTPS health checks, not just basic EC2 hypervisor checks.

options.text: Increase the idle timeout on the Application Load Balancer to 3600 seconds.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Increasing idle timeout keeps dead connections open longer without fixing replacement.

options.text: Disable health checks on the Application Load Balancer target group.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Disabling health checks causes ALB to route traffic to failed instances.

options.text: Assign public Elastic IP addresses directly to all EC2 instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Elastic IPs do not fix health check evaluation logic in Auto Scaling.

questions.generalExplanation: By default, Auto Scaling groups only check EC2 instance hardware status. Setting the health check type to ELB enables Auto Scaling to replace instances that fail application-level HTTP health checks.

questions.statement: A company needs a centralized service to automate and consolidate backup scheduling, retention policies, and cross-region backup copies across Amazon EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, and S3. Which service should they use?

options.text: AWS Backup
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Backup provides a centralized, policy-based backup service to automate data protection across AWS compute, database, and storage services.

options.text: AWS Data Pipeline
options.explanation: Incorrect: Data Pipeline is for batch data transformation workflows.

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudWatch Synthetics runs canary tests for endpoints.

options.text: AWS CloudFormation Drift Detection
options.explanation: Incorrect: Drift Detection checks template infrastructure drift.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Backup is a cost-effective, fully managed, policy-based service that simplifies data protection at scale across 15+ AWS services.

questions.statement: In an asynchronous message processing architecture, certain corrupt messages cause consumer worker applications to crash repeatedly, preventing them from completing processing. How can the architect isolate these problematic messages for debugging without blocking the main queue?

options.text: Configure an Amazon SQS Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) with a maxReceiveCount threshold.
options.explanation: Correct: A Dead-Letter Queue isolates unprocessable 'poison' messages after a specified number of failed processing attempts (maxReceiveCount), keeping the main queue flowing.

options.text: Increase the SQS message visibility timeout to 12 hours.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Increasing visibility timeout delays message reprocessing, but does not isolate bad messages.

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 Object Lock on the SQS queue.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Object Lock is an S3 feature, not an SQS queuing mechanism.

options.text: Switch the queue to Amazon SNS Fanout.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SNS Fanout broadcasts messages to multiple subscribers, multiplying the crash.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon SQS Dead-Letter Queues (DLQs) help isolate messages that cannot be processed successfully to analyze failure reasons and prevent blocking other valid messages.

questions.statement: A multinational mobile application requires a globally distributed database that provides multi-region active-active read and write capabilities with automatic multi-directional data replication and fast local read/write performance. Which database service meets this requirement?

options.text: Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables
options.explanation: Correct: DynamoDB Global Tables provide fully managed active-active multi-region replication, enabling applications to perform fast local reads and writes in multiple AWS Regions worldwide.

options.text: Amazon RDS for MySQL with a single cross-region Read Replica
options.explanation: Incorrect: RDS cross-region read replicas are read-only; they do not support active-active writes in secondary regions.

options.text: Amazon Redshift Multi-Node Cluster
options.explanation: Incorrect: Redshift is an analytics data warehouse, not an active-active global transactional NoSQL store.

options.text: Amazon DocumentDB with single instance storage
options.explanation: Incorrect: DocumentDB single instance does not support active-active global writes.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables build on DynamoDB's global footprint to provide fully managed, multi-region, multi-active databases for globally distributed applications.

questions.statement: How can an enterprise protect critical Amazon S3 objects from accidental permanent deletion or malicious overwriting, requiring hardware multi-factor authentication before an object version can be permanently removed?

options.text: Enable S3 Versioning and configure S3 MFA Delete on the bucket.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Versioning keeps historical versions of objects, and MFA Delete requires authentication from a physical MFA device to permanently delete an object version or change bucket versioning states.

options.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete expired delete markers every 30 days.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Expiring delete markers does not require MFA verification.

options.text: Attach an IAM policy with Action s3:* and Condition StringEquals on ec2:InstanceType.
options.explanation: Incorrect: This is invalid syntax and does not enforce MFA for S3 deletion.

options.text: Enable Amazon CloudWatch Detailed Monitoring on the bucket.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudWatch monitors metrics, it does not prevent object deletion.

questions.generalExplanation: S3 MFA Delete adds an extra layer of security on versioned S3 buckets: only the bucket owner using root credentials with MFA can permanently delete object versions.

questions.statement: A company wants to minimize disaster recovery costs for their on-premises physical and virtual servers. They need continuous block-level replication to AWS with an RPO of seconds and RTO of minutes without paying for full compute instances until a disaster is declared. Which AWS service is designed for this?

options.text: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS DRS)
options.explanation: Correct: AWS DRS continuously replicates physical and virtual machines at block level into low-cost staging storage, only provisioning full compute instances during failover tests or actual disasters.

options.text: AWS Snowball Edge
options.explanation: Incorrect: Snowball Edge is for physical data migration, not real-time continuous disaster recovery failover.

options.text: Amazon AppFlow
options.explanation: Incorrect: AppFlow integrates SaaS data transfers.

options.text: AWS CodePipeline
options.explanation: Incorrect: CodePipeline is a CI/CD automation tool.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS DRS) minimizes downtime and data loss with fast, reliable recovery of on-premises and cloud-based applications using affordable storage and minimal compute resources.

questions.statement: When creating a new Amazon EBS volume from a snapshot, instances experience I/O latency on initial blocks due to lazy loading from S3. How can an architect ensure that newly restored volumes immediately deliver maximum provisioned performance upon creation?

options.text: Enable Amazon EBS Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR) on the snapshot.
options.explanation: Correct: EBS Fast Snapshot Restore eliminates snapshot latency by pre-warming blocks so restored volumes instantly achieve maximum IOPS without initialization delay.

options.text: Change the volume type to Cold HDD (sc1).
options.explanation: Incorrect: Cold HDD has low throughput and does not solve block initialization latency.

options.text: Attach an Elastic IP directly to the EBS volume.
options.explanation: Incorrect: EBS volumes are block storage devices; they do not have IP addresses.

options.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the EC2 instance.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Transfer Acceleration is for long-distance S3 uploads, not EBS initialization.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon EBS Fast Snapshot Restore (FSR) enables you to restore EBS volumes from a snapshot that are fully initialized at creation time and instantly deliver all provisioned performance.

questions.statement: An IoT platform collects sensor telemetry from 50,000 vehicles using Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. During rush hour, data volume doubles, causing producer applications to receive ProvisionedThroughputExceededException errors. What is the quickest way to resolve this issue?

options.text: Increase the number of shards in the Kinesis Data Stream or switch the stream capacity mode to On-Demand.
options.explanation: Correct: Kinesis capacity is determined by shards (1 MB/sec in, 2 MB/sec out per shard) or On-Demand mode which automatically scales shard capacity to match throughput spikes.

options.text: Convert the stream into an S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval vault.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Glacier is an archive storage class, not a real-time streaming ingestion pipeline.

options.text: Decrease the message payload retention period from 24 hours to 1 hour.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Retention period affects storage duration, not per-second ingestion throughput capacity.

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer in front of the IoT vehicles.
options.explanation: Incorrect: ALBs do not resolve Kinesis Data Streams shard throughput limits.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams throughput is scaled by splitting shards or using On-Demand capacity mode, which automatically manages shard capacity in response to traffic changes.

questions.statement: A gaming company hosts multiplayer game servers on EC2 instances across multiple AWS Regions using UDP protocols. Players experience high packet loss and jitter over the public internet. The company needs static anycast IP addresses that route traffic over the AWS global private fiber network to the closest healthy endpoint. Which service should they use?

options.text: AWS Global Accelerator
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Global Accelerator provides 2 static Anycast IP addresses and routes TCP/UDP traffic over the AWS global fiber backbone to the nearest healthy regional endpoint.

options.text: Amazon CloudFront
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudFront is primarily designed for HTTP/HTTPS/WebSockets content caching, not raw UDP gaming packet acceleration.

options.text: Amazon Route 53 Simple Routing
options.explanation: Incorrect: Route 53 simple routing does not provide static anycast IP endpoints or private backbone routing.

options.text: AWS Storage Gateway
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage Gateway is a hybrid storage appliance.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network backbone and Anycast static IP addresses to optimize routing for TCP and UDP workloads like gaming, VoIP, and IoT.

questions.statement: A financial application processes loan applications through an intricate multi-step workflow involving credit checks, fraud detection, document validation, and human review approval steps that can take days. Which service should be used to coordinate these distributed microservices with built-in retry logic and state management?

options.text: AWS Step Functions
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Step Functions is a low-code visual workflow service used to orchestrate microservices, manage long-running stateful workflows, and handle retries and human approvals.

options.text: AWS CodeBuild
options.explanation: Incorrect: CodeBuild compiles and tests source code in CI/CD pipelines.

options.text: Amazon Simple Email Service (SES)
options.explanation: Incorrect: SES is an email delivery service.

options.text: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached
options.explanation: Incorrect: Memcached is an in-memory caching engine, not a workflow state machine.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Step Functions lets you coordinate multiple AWS services into serverless workflows with error handling, branching, and support for executions that can run up to 1 year.

questions.statement: A stock trading platform requires that financial transactions are processed strictly in the exact order they are received, with guaranteed exactly-once processing (no duplicate transactions). Which queuing solution must be used?

options.text: Amazon SQS FIFO (First-In-First-Out) Queue
options.explanation: Correct: SQS FIFO queues preserve the exact order of messages and support deduplication to ensure messages are processed exactly once in strict chronological order.

options.text: Amazon SQS Standard Queue
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard queues provide at-least-once delivery (duplicates possible) and best-effort ordering.

options.text: Amazon SNS Standard Topic
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard SNS topics do not guarantee strict message ordering or exactly-once delivery.

options.text: Amazon S3 Event Notifications
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 event notifications do not guarantee strict sequential message delivery order.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon SQS FIFO queues have the .fifo suffix and guarantee that message order is strictly preserved with exactly-once processing and deduplication.

questions.statement: An architect needs to ensure that when an EC2 instance is terminated by Auto Scaling, a custom script exports local log files to an Amazon S3 bucket and gracefully unregisters background worker tasks before the instance is shut down. Which Auto Scaling feature enables this?

options.text: Auto Scaling Lifecycle Hooks
options.explanation: Correct: Lifecycle hooks pause the termination or launch of an instance, putting it in a Terminating:Wait state to allow custom scripts or Lambda functions to complete before final termination.

options.text: EC2 User Data scripts
options.explanation: Incorrect: User Data scripts execute only upon instance initial launch/boot, not termination.

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor
options.explanation: Incorrect: Trusted Advisor performs best practice evaluations, not instance shutdown lifecycle hooks.

options.text: Elastic Load Balancing Sticky Sessions
options.explanation: Incorrect: Sticky sessions bind user sessions to specific instances.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling Lifecycle Hooks give you control over instances as they enter and leave an Auto Scaling group, enabling custom log harvesting or graceful connection draining before termination.

questions.statement: A news web application with high read volume and low write volume is experiencing database performance degradation due to repetitive SQL queries on an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Which solution will improve read performance most cost-effectively and quickly?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of Amazon RDS and implement a Lazy Loading (Cache-Aside) caching strategy.
options.explanation: Correct: In-memory ElastiCache dramatically reduces read latency to sub-milliseconds and offloads repetitive read queries from the relational database.

options.text: Migrate the RDS database to larger instance types with io2 Block Express EBS volumes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Vertical scaling with io2 is far more expensive and does not solve repetitive in-memory caching efficiency.

options.text: Enable Multi-AZ on RDS and direct SELECT queries to the secondary standby instance.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Traditional RDS Multi-AZ standby instances are passive for failover and do not accept read traffic (unlike Aurora or dedicated Read Replicas).

options.text: Enable AWS Auto Scaling directly on the RDS MySQL primary node.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard RDS MySQL single instances do not support instantaneous on-demand compute node auto-scaling for reads like ElastiCache.

questions.generalExplanation: An in-memory caching layer with Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) using the Cache-Aside pattern is the recommended AWS best practice for read-heavy relational database workloads.

questions.statement: An analytics application writes and reads millions of small files to an Amazon S3 bucket, reaching 15,000 GET requests per second. How can the application optimize request throughput on Amazon S3 without incurring extra service fees?

options.text: Distribute objects across multiple distinct S3 key prefixes to achieve up to 5,500 GET requests/sec per prefix.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 automatically scales to support at least 3,500 PUT/POST/DELETE and 5,500 GET/HEAD requests per second per partitioned prefix.

options.text: Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication to 10 different regions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: CRR replicates objects across regions, but does not increase per-prefix throughput in the source bucket.

options.text: Combine all files into a single 5 TB object stored in S3 Glacier.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Glacier has retrieval times of minutes to hours and does not support high-concurrency real-time reads.

options.text: Attach an Elastic Load Balancer directly in front of the S3 bucket endpoint.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Elastic Load Balancers cannot be placed in front of Amazon S3 buckets.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 scales automatically to handle high request rates: each distinct prefix supports at least 3,500 write requests and 5,500 read requests per second.

questions.statement: A critical enterprise database on Amazon EC2 requires consistent 40,000 IOPS and sub-millisecond I/O latency for heavy transactional read/write workloads. Which Amazon EBS volume type should be chosen?

options.text: Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 or io2 Block Express)
options.explanation: Correct: io2 / io2 Block Express volumes are designed for business-critical I/O intensive databases requiring up to 256,000 IOPS and sub-millisecond latency with 99.999% durability.

options.text: General Purpose SSD (gp3)
options.explanation: Incorrect: gp3 maxes out at 16,000 IOPS, which cannot meet the 40,000 IOPS requirement.

options.text: Throughput Optimized HDD (st1)
options.explanation: Incorrect: st1 is magnetic storage optimized for throughput (MB/s) on large sequential workloads, not high random IOPS.

options.text: Cold HDD (sc1)
options.explanation: Incorrect: sc1 is low-cost magnetic storage for infrequently accessed sequential workloads.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2 Block Express) volumes deliver the highest performance block storage on AWS, supporting up to 256,000 IOPS and 4,000 MB/s throughput.

questions.statement: Users around the world upload large 10 GB video files to a centralized Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1. Users in Europe and Asia report high upload latency. What is the most effective solution to accelerate global uploads to S3?

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket and use the accelerated endpoint for uploads.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses Amazon CloudFront's globally distributed Edge Locations to route uploads over the optimized AWS private network backbone to the S3 bucket.

options.text: Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN from every user's computer to us-east-1.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Creating individual VPN tunnels for end consumers across the globe is impractical.

options.text: Deploy NAT Gateways in Europe and Asia connected to us-east-1.
options.explanation: Incorrect: NAT Gateways are deployed inside VPCs, not for global public consumer uploads.

options.text: Require users to compress videos into zip files and email them to AWS Support.
options.explanation: Incorrect: This is an unfeasible operational anti-pattern.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration enables fast, easy, and secure transfers of files over long distances between your client and an S3 bucket by utilizing AWS Edge Locations.

questions.statement: A genomics research lab runs High Performance Computing (HPC) simulations on hundreds of EC2 instances that require a POSIX-compliant distributed file system capable of processing sub-millisecond latencies and hundreds of gigabytes per second of throughput linked directly with Amazon S3. Which service should they choose?

options.text: Amazon FSx for Lustre
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon FSx for Lustre is built for high-performance computing (HPC), machine learning, and media rendering, integrating natively with S3 buckets for high-throughput sub-millisecond shared storage.

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
options.explanation: Incorrect: FSx for Windows is designed for SMB-based Windows enterprise workloads.

options.text: AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
options.explanation: Incorrect: Tape Gateway is for long-term virtual tape archives.

options.text: Amazon EFS One Zone
options.explanation: Incorrect: EFS One Zone does not match the extreme hundreds-of-GB/s parallel throughput of Lustre for HPC.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed file system optimized for compute-intensive workloads such as high-performance computing, machine learning, and data analytics.

questions.statement: An engineering firm needs to run tightly coupled node-to-node MPI (Message Passing Interface) simulations across a fleet of EC2 instances requiring the lowest possible network latency and highest packet-per-second performance. Which placement group strategy should they configure?

options.text: Cluster Placement Group
options.explanation: Correct: A Cluster Placement Group packs instances close together inside a single Availability Zone to achieve low-latency network performance up to 100 Gbps.

options.text: Spread Placement Group
options.explanation: Incorrect: Spread placement groups strictly separate instances across distinct hardware racks to minimize correlated failures.

options.text: Partition Placement Group
options.explanation: Incorrect: Partition placement groups divide instances across logical partitions for large distributed workloads like HDFS/Cassandra.

options.text: Multi-Region Global Group
options.explanation: Incorrect: Placement groups operate within a single region, not cross-region.

questions.generalExplanation: A Cluster Placement Group is a logical grouping of instances within a single Availability Zone that enables applications to participate in a low-latency, high-throughput network.

questions.statement: An online auction website using Amazon DynamoDB receives extreme surges in read traffic on trending items, causing read latency spikes. The development team needs an in-memory caching tier that provides microsecond read response times without rewriting application query code. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
options.explanation: Correct: DAX is a fully managed, highly available, in-memory cache for DynamoDB that delivers up to a 10x performance improvement (from milliseconds to microseconds) and is API-compatible without code refactoring.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Redshift cluster and replicate data every hour.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Redshift is an analytics warehouse with second-level query latency, not a microsecond cache.

options.text: Switch DynamoDB to Provisioned Billing with autoscaling.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Provisioned billing handles millisecond reads, but does not provide in-memory microsecond caching without code changes.

options.text: Migrate all data to an Amazon RDS MySQL database with Multi-AZ.
options.explanation: Incorrect: RDS requires full application query rewrites and does not deliver microsecond latency.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is an in-memory cache that reduces DynamoDB response times to microseconds and is drop-in compatible with existing DynamoDB API calls.

questions.statement: A reporting application runs heavy read-only analytical queries against an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster, impacting the performance of live user transactions on the primary writer node. How can the Solutions Architect isolate the reporting workload?

options.text: Create an Aurora Read Replica and point the reporting application to the cluster's Reader Endpoint or a custom endpoint.
options.explanation: Correct: Reader Endpoints load balance read queries across available Aurora Read Replicas, isolating read queries completely from the primary read/write instance.

options.text: Convert the primary database to Single-AZ mode.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Single-AZ reduces availability and does not solve read contention.

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 Object Lock on the database storage volume.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Object Lock is an S3 feature and does not apply to Aurora compute queries.

options.text: Replace the Aurora cluster with an Amazon EBS magnetic volume.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Magnetic volumes provide inferior performance and lack relational engine capabilities.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Aurora provides a dedicated Reader Endpoint that distributes read-only traffic across all provisioned Aurora Replicas, offloading read load from the primary writer node.

questions.statement: A microservices application built with AWS Lambda experiences intermittent high latency ('cold starts') when functions are invoked after periods of inactivity. How can the architect guarantee low, single-digit millisecond invocation latencies at all times?

options.text: Configure Provisioned Concurrency for the AWS Lambda functions.
options.explanation: Correct: Provisioned Concurrency keeps a specified number of execution environments initialized and hyper-ready to respond immediately in double-digit milliseconds, eliminating cold starts.

options.text: Increase the Lambda function timeout setting from 3 seconds to 15 minutes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Function timeout limits maximum execution duration; it does not eliminate cold start initialization delay.

options.text: Migrate the Lambda functions to run on an Amazon Lightsail instance.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Lightsail is a virtual server VPS, removing serverless benefits and scalability.

options.text: Attach an Elastic IP directly to the Lambda function.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Lambda functions cannot have Elastic IPs attached directly.

questions.generalExplanation: Provisioned Concurrency initializes requested execution environments ahead of time so they can respond immediately without cold start initialization latencies.

questions.statement: An Amazon EC2 instance running network-intensive packet inspection software is experiencing high inter-instance latency and jitter. Which feature should be enabled on the EC2 instance to provide single-root I/O virtualization (SR-IOV) and up to 100 Gbps network performance?

options.text: Enhanced Networking using the Elastic Network Adapter (ENA)
options.explanation: Correct: Enhanced Networking uses SR-IOV to bypass the hypervisor and provide higher I/O performance and lower CPU utilization with speeds up to 100 Gbps.

options.text: Elastic IP dynamic reassignment
options.explanation: Incorrect: Elastic IPs manage public IPv4 addresses, not network hardware acceleration.

options.text: Amazon S3 Select acceleration
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Select filters CSV/JSON data inside S3, not EC2 network interfaces.

options.text: AWS Direct Connect gateway aggregation
options.explanation: Incorrect: Direct Connect connects on-premises networks to AWS.

questions.generalExplanation: Enhanced Networking uses Single Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV) via the Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) to deliver high packets-per-second (PPS) and low latency.

questions.statement: An e-commerce company needs to provide real-time full-text search, auto-complete suggestions, and faceted filtering across a catalog of 20 million products with sub-second response times. Which managed AWS service is purpose-built for this use case?

options.text: Amazon OpenSearch Service (successor to Amazon Elasticsearch Service)
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon OpenSearch Service provides managed full-text search, analytics, log indexing, and auto-complete indexing with high concurrency and sub-second latencies.

options.text: Amazon Athena
options.explanation: Incorrect: Athena is for interactive SQL analytics on S3, not sub-second interactive full-text web search.

options.text: AWS Glue DataBrew
options.explanation: Incorrect: DataBrew is a visual data preparation tool.

options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is an archive storage tier.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service makes it easy to perform interactive log analytics, real-time application monitoring, website search, and full-text querying at scale.

questions.statement: A multinational corporation operates identical production environments in us-east-1, eu-central-1, and ap-southeast-1. They want users to be automatically directed to the AWS Region that provides the lowest network latency for their individual connection. Which Route 53 routing policy should be configured?

options.text: Latency-based Routing
options.explanation: Correct: Latency-based routing directs user DNS queries to the AWS Region that gives the lowest network latency based on AWS worldwide network measurements.

options.text: Weighted Routing with equal weights (33/33/33)
options.explanation: Incorrect: Weighted routing distributes traffic evenly regardless of user geographic location or network latency.

options.text: Simple Routing with multiple IP addresses
options.explanation: Incorrect: Simple routing returns IP addresses in random order without evaluating network performance.

options.text: Failover Routing with passive replicas
options.explanation: Incorrect: Failover routing is for active-passive disaster recovery, not multi-region performance optimization.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Route 53 Latency-based Routing routes traffic to the AWS Region that provides the best latency for the user, improving application performance globally.

questions.statement: A data analytics team uses Amazon Athena to query 50 TB of web clickstream logs stored in Amazon S3. Queries are taking several minutes to complete and incurring high costs because Athena scans the entire dataset for every query. Which TWO techniques will significantly reduce query execution time and cost? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Partition the data in Amazon S3 by year, month, and day (e.g., year=2026/month=08/day=20/).
options.explanation: Correct: Partitioning limits the amount of data Athena scans per query to only the relevant date folders, dramatically cutting query time and scanned byte costs.

options.text: Convert the data files into columnar formats such as Apache Parquet or Apache ORC.
options.explanation: Correct: Columnar formats (Parquet/ORC) allow Athena to read only the required columns and compress data efficiently, reducing I/O and query costs by up to 90%.

options.text: Store all data in uncompressed JSON format in a single root folder.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storing uncompressed single-folder data forces Athena to scan all 50 TB for every query.

options.text: Change S3 bucket versioning to MFA Delete mode.
options.explanation: Incorrect: MFA Delete is a security feature that has no impact on SQL query scanning performance.

options.text: Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication to 5 other regions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Replication increases storage costs and does not optimize Athena query scanning.

questions.generalExplanation: Partitioning data and converting files to columnar formats (Parquet or ORC) are the two most effective strategies to optimize Athena query performance and reduce scanning costs.

questions.statement: A media streaming website with global CloudFront distribution observes that cache misses across 400+ Edge Locations cause high concurrent load on the origin web servers in us-east-1. How can they reduce origin server load during cache misses?

options.text: Enable CloudFront Origin Shield in us-east-1.
options.explanation: Correct: Origin Shield acts as a centralized caching layer between CloudFront edge locations and your origin, consolidating requests and minimizing origin load.

options.text: Create an S3 bucket in each edge location.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 buckets exist in AWS Regions, not inside CloudFront edge locations.

options.text: Disable CloudFront caching completely.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Disabling caching routes 100% of traffic to the origin, worsening the problem.

options.text: Configure Route 53 Weighted routing to random instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Weighted routing does not provide edge caching consolidation.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon CloudFront Origin Shield is a centralized caching layer that minimizes your origin's load, improves cache hit ratios, and reduces operating costs.

questions.statement: An Amazon EC2 instance requires a single file system with 80,000 IOPS and 1,500 MB/s throughput, but the maximum single EBS gp3 volume throughput is limited. Assuming backup snapshots are handled at application level, how can storage IOPS and throughput be aggregated across multiple EBS volumes on a single instance?

options.text: Attach multiple EBS volumes and configure a software RAID 0 array inside the operating system.
options.explanation: Correct: RAID 0 stripes data across multiple EBS volumes, combining their IOPS and throughput up to the EC2 instance's maximum EBS-optimized bandwidth.

options.text: Configure a software RAID 1 array across multiple EBS volumes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: RAID 1 mirrors data for redundancy; it does not aggregate write throughput.

options.text: Store data in an Amazon S3 Glacier Vault.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Glacier is cold archival storage, not high-speed OS block storage.

options.text: Attach an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cached mode.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage Gateway cached mode is for hybrid on-premises access.

questions.generalExplanation: Configuring a software RAID 0 array across multiple EBS volumes allows you to stripe I/O and achieve higher throughput and IOPS than a single EBS volume can provide.

questions.statement: A healthcare provider generates medical scan images that need to be accessed frequently for the first 30 days. After 30 days, images are rarely accessed but must be retained for 5 years due to legal compliance, with a retrieval time of up to 5 hours acceptable. What is the most cost-effective Amazon S3 lifecycle strategy?

options.text: Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days, and expire/delete them after 5 years.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Standard covers initial active access, while S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval provides low-cost long-term storage for 3-5 hour retrieval requirements.

options.text: Store all files in S3 Glacier Deep Archive from the start with expedited retrieval.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Glacier Deep Archive does not support initial frequent access and does not offer expedited retrieval.

options.text: Transition objects to S3 One Zone-IA after 30 days and retain for 5 years.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 One Zone-IA has higher storage costs than Glacier and lower resilience (single AZ), which is not suitable for critical medical data.

options.text: Keep objects in S3 Standard and manually apply gzip compression after 30 days.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Keeping files in S3 Standard for 5 years incurs excessive costs and manual compression creates high operational overhead.

questions.generalExplanation: Automated transition via S3 Lifecycle to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval minimizes long-term storage costs while maintaining compliant availability within acceptable retrieval timeframes.

questions.statement: A data analytics company runs a nightly batch video rendering job that takes 4 hours to complete. The job is fault-tolerant and can resume from checkpoints if interrupted. Which EC2 instance purchasing strategy delivers the lowest compute cost?

options.text: Run the rendering fleet on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group with a diversified instance type allocation strategy.
options.explanation: Correct: Spot instances offer up to 90% cost savings compared to On-Demand, perfectly matching interruption-tolerant and checkpointed batch processing jobs.

options.text: Purchase 3-year All Upfront Dedicated Hosts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive EC2 purchasing option and lock up capital.

options.text: Launch On-Demand Instances with EBS io2 Block Express volumes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: On-Demand pricing is significantly more expensive than Spot for batch jobs.

options.text: Purchase 1-year Standard Reserved Instances for maximum nightly capacity.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Paying 24/7 for Reserved Instances that only run 4 hours per night results in significant wasted idle cost.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon EC2 Spot Instances offer up to 90% savings over On-Demand pricing, making them ideal for fault-tolerant, stateless, or checkpointed batch processing workloads.

questions.statement: An enterprise plans to modernize its compute infrastructure over the next 3 years, moving portions of their workloads from EC2 instances (across multiple instance families and regions) to AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda. Which pricing model offers flexible cost savings across all these compute services?

options.text: Compute Savings Plans
options.explanation: Correct: Compute Savings Plans provide up to 66% discount and automatically apply across EC2 instances (regardless of family, OS, or region), AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda.

options.text: EC2 Instance Savings Plans
options.explanation: Incorrect: EC2 Instance Savings Plans are locked to a specific instance family in a specific region and do not apply to Fargate or Lambda.

options.text: Standard Reserved Instances
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard RIs do not apply to Fargate or Lambda and lack cross-family/cross-region flexibility.

options.text: On-Demand Capacity Reservations
options.explanation: Incorrect: Capacity Reservations reserve capacity at On-Demand rates without providing billing discounts.

questions.generalExplanation: Compute Savings Plans provide the greatest flexibility, automatically reducing costs across EC2 instance families, operating systems, regions, and container/serverless services (Fargate and Lambda).

questions.statement: A company notices high monthly data processing charges on their AWS NAT Gateways. Analysis reveals that 90% of the traffic is from private EC2 instances downloading packages and objects from Amazon S3 and DynamoDB. How can the company eliminate these NAT Gateway data processing charges?

options.text: Create a Gateway VPC Endpoint for Amazon S3 and a Gateway VPC Endpoint for Amazon DynamoDB in the VPC.
options.explanation: Correct: Gateway VPC Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are provided at no hourly or data processing charge, routing private traffic directly to S3/DynamoDB without passing through NAT Gateways.

options.text: Replace the NAT Gateways with an Internet Gateway in each private subnet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Internet Gateways cannot be attached to private subnets without assigning public IPs.

options.text: Move all EC2 instances to public subnets.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Moving instances to public subnets exposes them directly to internet security threats.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Site-to-Site VPN to loop traffic back through on-premises firewalls.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Looping through on-premises incurs massive egress and VPN transfer costs.

questions.generalExplanation: Gateway VPC Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are completely free and allow traffic to bypass costly NAT Gateways, eliminating per-GB NAT data processing charges.

questions.statement: A company currently has 200 Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD (gp2) volumes attached to EC2 instances. How can they immediately reduce storage costs by up to 20% while gaining the ability to independently scale IOPS and throughput without provisioning larger disk sizes?

options.text: Migrate the volumes from gp2 to General Purpose SSD (gp3) using Elastic Volumes.
options.explanation: Correct: gp3 volumes are up to 20% cheaper per GB than gp2, provide baseline 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s throughput, and allow independent provisioning of IOPS/throughput without increasing disk size.

options.text: Convert all volumes to Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2).
options.explanation: Incorrect: io2 volumes are significantly more expensive than gp2/gp3.

options.text: Create snapshots and delete the original EBS volumes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Deleting active volumes breaks running applications.

options.text: Move data to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Glacier Deep Archive cannot be attached as live block storage to EC2.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon EBS gp3 volumes offer up to 20% lower price per GB than gp2 and provide baseline performance of 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s included with any volume size.

questions.statement: A human resources software company runs a relational database that is heavily utilized Monday through Friday during business hours, but sits virtually idle on nights and weekends. Which cost-optimized database solution automatically scales compute capacity up and down in fine increments based on actual demand?

options.text: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2
options.explanation: Correct: Aurora Serverless v2 scales compute capacity dynamically in fractions of an ACU (Aurora Capacity Unit) in milliseconds, paying only for database capacity consumed during active usage.

options.text: Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ provisioned with db.m5.24xlarge instances 24/7
options.explanation: Incorrect: Fixed provisioned large instances incur continuous high costs during nights and weekends.

options.text: Amazon Redshift with fixed 16-node cluster
options.explanation: Incorrect: Redshift is an analytics data warehouse and fixed clusters incur constant hourly billing.

options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Vault
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Glacier is an archive storage tier, not an active transactional relational database.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Aurora Serverless v2 adjusts database capacity in fine-grained increments in fractions of a second to match workload demand, saving up to 90% compared to provisioning for peak capacity.

questions.statement: An operations team manages hundreds of EC2 instances and EBS volumes. They need automated, ML-driven recommendations to identify over-provisioned (idle/oversized) instances and right-size them to optimal instance types. Which service provides this?

options.text: AWS Compute Optimizer
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning to analyze historical CloudWatch utilization metrics and delivers actionable right-sizing recommendations for EC2, EBS, Lambda, and ECS.

options.text: AWS CodeDeploy
options.explanation: Incorrect: CodeDeploy automates code deployments.

options.text: Amazon CloudFront
options.explanation: Incorrect: CloudFront is a content delivery network.

options.text: AWS KMS
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS KMS manages cryptographic encryption keys.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Compute Optimizer recommends optimal AWS resources for your workloads to reduce costs by up to 25% by analyzing historical utilization metrics.

questions.statement: A legal firm must retain 500 TB of closed case documentation for 10 years to comply with regulatory mandates. The files are almost never accessed, and a retrieval timeframe of 12 hours is acceptable. Which storage option offers the lowest cost per gigabyte in the cloud?

options.text: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost storage class in the cloud (under $1 per TB/month), designed for long-term retention of data retrieved within 12 hours.

options.text: Amazon S3 Standard
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Standard is designed for active frequent access and costs over 20x more per GB than Glacier Deep Archive.

options.text: Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) Standard
options.explanation: Incorrect: EFS is a high-performance interactive file system with significantly higher storage costs.

options.text: Amazon EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2)
options.explanation: Incorrect: EBS io2 is high-performance block storage, unsuitable and cost-prohibitive for 500 TB cold archives.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive is Amazon S3's lowest-cost storage class, designed for long-term retention of data accessed once or twice a year.

questions.statement: A company wants to automatically detect unexpected sudden cost spikes caused by rogue deployments or infinite loop scripts, receiving root cause analysis via email or Slack in near real-time. Which tool should they configure?

options.text: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses advanced machine learning models to identify unexpected spending anomalies and cost drivers, delivering alert notifications with root cause analysis.

options.text: AWS Pricing Calculator
options.explanation: Incorrect: Pricing Calculator is a pre-deployment cost modeling tool.

options.text: AWS Shield Standard
options.explanation: Incorrect: Shield Standard is for DDoS attack mitigation.

options.text: Amazon Lex
options.explanation: Incorrect: Lex builds conversational chatbots.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to continuously monitor cost and usage patterns to detect anomalous spending events and identify root causes.

questions.statement: A popular website hosted on EC2 instances serves static video thumbnails to millions of international users directly from web servers, resulting in heavy Amazon EC2 Internet Data Transfer Out charges. How can the company significantly reduce data transfer costs while improving latency?
