options.text: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the web servers to cache thumbnails at edge locations.
options.explanation: Correct: CloudFront caches static content at global edge locations, drastically reducing EC2 egress traffic. Data transfer from AWS origins to CloudFront is free, and CloudFront egress rates are lower than direct EC2 internet egress.

options.text: Configure an AWS Direct Connect 10 Gbps dedicated connection for all end users.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Direct Connect cannot connect millions of individual global public internet consumers.

options.text: Attach Elastic IP addresses to all EC2 instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Elastic IPs do not reduce internet data egress bandwidth charges.

options.text: Switch all EC2 instances to Windows Server Bare Metal instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Bare metal instances increase compute and licensing costs without reducing egress traffic.

questions.generalExplanation: Using Amazon CloudFront reduces data transfer out costs because data transferred from AWS origins (EC2, S3, ALB) to CloudFront edge locations is free of charge, and CDN egress rates are discounted.

questions.statement: A web startup runs open-source Python and Node.js microservices on x86-based EC2 instances (m5.large). How can the engineering team reduce compute costs by up to 20% and achieve up to 40% better price-performance with minimal code modification?

options.text: Migrate the microservices to AWS Graviton-based instance families (e.g., m7g or c7g).
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Graviton processors (custom ARM64 silicon) offer up to 40% better price-performance over comparable x86 instances for Linux workloads running open-source runtimes like Python, Node.js, and Java.

options.text: Upgrade to larger x86 instances with GPU accelerators (p4d.24xlarge).
options.explanation: Incorrect: GPU instances are designed for ML training and are vastly more expensive.

options.text: Deploy all microservices into Amazon S3 Glacier vaults.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Glacier is an archive storage tier, not a compute execution runtime.

options.text: Disable multi-threading in the Linux kernel on current m5 instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Disabling hyperthreading reduces throughput without reducing instance hourly costs.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Graviton processors deliver major cost savings and price-performance improvements for cloud workloads built on Linux and open-source stacks.

questions.statement: An organization with hundreds of AWS accounts and petabytes of data across thousands of S3 buckets needs organization-wide visibility into storage usage, activity trends, and cost-optimization recommendations (such as identifying non-current versions or incomplete multipart uploads). Which tool provides this?

options.text: Amazon S3 Storage Lens
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Storage Lens is a cloud storage analytics feature providing organization-wide visibility into object storage usage, cost optimization metrics, and data protection insights.

options.text: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
options.explanation: Incorrect: Patch Manager automates OS patching on servers.

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics
options.explanation: Incorrect: Synthetics monitors website REST APIs.

options.text: AWS IAM Access Analyzer
options.explanation: Incorrect: IAM Access Analyzer identifies resources shared with external entities.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Storage Lens provides centralized visibility and actionable recommendations to optimize storage costs across all buckets and accounts in an AWS Organization.

questions.statement: A company uploads thousands of large objects to Amazon S3 using multipart uploads. Occasionally, network interruptions cause uploads to fail before all parts are received, leaving incomplete multipart parts accumulating storage fees indefinitely. How can the architect automate the cleanup of incomplete multipart uploads to eliminate these costs?

options.text: Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule with the action AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload to abort and delete incomplete parts after a specified number of days.
options.explanation: Correct: The AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle action automatically deletes partial parts of incomplete multipart uploads after a specified retention window (e.g., 7 days), preventing hidden storage costs.

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 Object Lock in Governance mode.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Object Lock prevents deletion, which would keep incomplete parts forever.

options.text: Write a daily cron script on an EC2 instance that runs aws s3 rm on all buckets.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard s3 rm does not delete hidden incomplete multipart upload parts.

options.text: Convert the bucket to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Changing storage class does not abort incomplete multipart uploads.

questions.generalExplanation: Configuring an S3 Lifecycle rule to abort incomplete multipart uploads is an AWS Well-Architected cost optimization best practice to prevent uncompleted upload parts from consuming billable storage.
